post.author: Christine Gwinnup
post.body:
Summer is almost here, and it's the perfect time to get your home ready for the warmer months. From boosting curb appeal to making your home more energy-efficient, these tips will help you create a welcoming and comfortable environment for the season. Whether you're planning to sell or simply want to enjoy your space, here are some expert suggestions to prepare your home for summer.

Enhance Your Curb Appeal

Refresh Your Landscaping

Summer is the season for lush greenery and vibrant flowers. Start by mowing the lawn, trimming hedges, and weeding flower beds. Consider planting colorful annuals or perennials to add a pop of color to your yard. Incorporate native plants that thrive in the local climate, which can reduce water usage and maintenance. Adding mulch to flower beds not only retains moisture but also gives a neat appearance.

Clean and Paint the Exterior

Give your home a fresh look by power washing the exterior and cleaning windows. This helps remove dirt, grime, and mildew that can build up over time. If your home’s paint is peeling or faded, consider giving it a new coat. A freshly painted front door in a bold color can also make a great first impression. Don’t forget to clean gutters and downspouts to ensure they are free of debris and functioning properly.

Optimize Outdoor Living Spaces

Upgrade Your Patio or Deck

Summer is perfect for outdoor entertaining. Ensure your patio or deck is in good condition by repairing any damaged areas and giving it a thorough cleaning. Sand and reseal wood surfaces to protect them from the elements. Adding comfortable seating, outdoor rugs, and lighting can transform your outdoor space into an inviting retreat. Consider adding shade options like umbrellas, pergolas, or awnings to make the space usable even on the hottest days.

Create a Functional Garden Area

If you have a garden, consider creating a dedicated area for relaxation. Set up a small table and chairs, add some decorative elements, and make it a place where you can enjoy the beauty of your plants. Planting a mix of vegetables, herbs, and flowers can create a vibrant and productive garden. Raised beds or container gardening are great options for small spaces and can add visual interest to your yard.

Improve Indoor Comfort and Efficiency

Service Your Air Conditioning

Ensure your air conditioning system is running efficiently by scheduling a professional maintenance check. Clean or replace filters to improve air quality and reduce energy consumption. Regular maintenance can also help prevent breakdowns during the peak of summer heat. Consider investing in a programmable thermostat to optimize cooling when you’re home and save energy when you’re away.

Install Ceiling Fans

Ceiling fans can help circulate air and reduce reliance on air conditioning. They are a cost-effective way to keep your home cool and comfortable. When selecting ceiling fans, choose energy-efficient models and consider installing them in key areas like bedrooms and living spaces for maximum benefit.

Make Your Home More Energy-Efficient

Seal Windows and Doors

Check for drafts around windows and doors and seal any gaps with weatherstripping or caulk. This can help keep cool air inside and reduce energy costs. Consider adding thermal curtains or blinds to further insulate your home and block out the heat from the sun.

Upgrade to Energy-Efficient Appliances

If your appliances are outdated, consider upgrading to energy-efficient models. This can significantly reduce your energy bills and is an attractive feature for potential buyers. Look for appliances with the ENERGY STAR label, which meet strict energy efficiency guidelines set by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

Declutter and Organize

Clean Out Closets and Storage Spaces

Take advantage of the summer season to declutter your home. Clean out closets, organize storage spaces, and donate items you no longer need. A tidy home feels more spacious and inviting. This is also a great time to organize your garage and outdoor storage, ensuring that summer tools and equipment are easily accessible.

Rearrange Furniture for Better Flow

Consider rearranging your furniture to create a more open and airy feel. This can improve the flow of your home and make it more comfortable for summer living. Removing heavy drapes and opting for lighter window treatments can enhance natural light, making your home feel brighter and more welcoming.

Getting your home ready for summer doesn’t have to be a daunting task. By following these tips, you can enhance your home’s appeal, improve its efficiency, and create a more enjoyable living environment. Whether you're planning to sell or simply want to make the most of the season, these preparations will ensure your home is summer-ready.

For homeowners thinking about selling, implementing these tips can significantly boost your home's value and attract potential buyers, leading to a higher selling price.
